name: ActiveCampaign
summary: Marketing automation and lifecycle email with a light CRM attached.
best_for: businesses that want deep marketing automation and lifecycle email tied to a light CRM, and will actually use the automation depth
skip_if: you just need to send a newsletter — a simpler, cheaper email tool does that without paying for automation you won't touch
honest_knock: Pricing climbs with contact count and the add-ons (CRM, SMS, extra seats) stack up fast — the sticker Starter price is not what a serious automation setup actually costs. Powerful, but budget for the tier (Plus and up) you'll really use.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-08-17 and again 2026-09-29 in the browser; the figures below are the 'starts at' prices on annual billing, before you pick a contact count) No free plan, trial only. There are four tiers. Starter is from $15/mo with 1 user, limited segmentation and 5 actions per automation. Plus is from $49/mo with 1 user, standard segmentation, unlimited automation actions and landing pages. Pro is from $79/mo with 3 users, advanced segmentation, predictive and conditional content and attribution tracking. Enterprise is from $145/mo with 5 users, premium segmentation, SSO, custom objects and a dedicated account team. Your email send allowance is a multiple of your contact count — 10x on Starter and Plus, 12x on Pro, 15x on Enterprise. The bill then scales with list size, and the ladder only renders after you select a contact count: at 10,000 contacts on 2026-09-29 it read Starter $149, Plus $189, Pro $375 and Enterprise $589 a month on annual billing. A separate Email + WhatsApp plan starts at $112 (Plus), $142 (Pro) and $284 (Enterprise) a month, each with up to 5 WhatsApp lines. CRM pipelines, SMS and extra users remain paid add-ons.

sessions.what: On 30 September 2026 we opened a new ActiveCampaign account on the 14-day free trial, which carries the Pro plan's features, and gave Active Intelligence 3.0: Wavelength ten tasks: a brand kit from our website, a campaign from one of our test pages (twice), a Dutch translation, an image, a welcome automation, a daily scheduled task, industry benchmarks and an automation health check. We checked every result against our own pages, saved before it read them.
findings: On the empty account it said plainly that there were no campaigns in the past 12 months and no sends to compare with benchmarks, instead of inventing a best performer or figures.

Given one of our test pages, it wrote a complete campaign in about three minutes. All ten figures in it came from the page and none was added. The same prompt in a new conversation produced a different layout with one sentence the page does not support.

The Brand Kit it built from our homepage matched our voice, mission and colours, but it saved a blue 'N' logo that is not ours, which then appeared in every email, and it picked products we review as competitors.
The Dutch translation was fluent and wrote 250,000 as 250.000, but it replaced the English campaign and left a typo in the preheader and one mistranslated term.

It built a clean welcome automation (three emails, two three-day waits) in about a minute. Its health check then flagged the inactive status but missed that every email still needed a postal address and that nothing fed the new list.

The chat said it could not generate images, and the image generator in the Content Manager returned nothing in five attempts on 30 September 2026, nor in three more on 3 and 5 October. The AI Actions Library is locked in the trial until you buy Activities.

The daily scheduled task sent its first report on the morning of 1 October 2026. It described the new account correctly (one contact, no deals, nothing sent yet), but under competitors it summarised news from G2, Capterra and TrustRadius instead of the three competitors in our Brand Kit.
sessions.not_tested: One account, one morning, one run per task (two for the campaign). Real sends and deliverability, content performance with a send history and the limits of Starter and Plus remain untested.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

open_questions.question: Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?
